title: Simple partial differential equations can show complex behavior

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Simple partial differential equations can show complex behavior

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Complex behavior of the kind seen in simple programs is not restricted to discrete systems: some fairly simple partial differential equations, found by searching, produce highly complex patterns, even with apparently discrete patches.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we now know that the same kind of behavior can also occur in completely continuous systems such as partial differential equations.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Partial Differential Equations” (from p. 161), p. 164. Scope: one-dimensional nonlinear partial differential equations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-25: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.83

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The core is existential and can be confirmed by one reproducible PDE example that survives numerical convergence tests. Public solvers, benchmarks, and literature make the required analysis feasible with standard specialist methods.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Numerically integrate specified low-description-length nonlinear PDEs with convergence, precision, and perturbation checks, then quantify spatiotemporal complexity and patch persistence. A robust example confirms that such behavior can occur in a continuous PDE; failure under refinement identifies numerical artifacts.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Numerical discretization can generate false complexity.

Fairly simple and highly complex need declared measures.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.78

analysis feasibility: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is an existence claim about continuous equations, and public solvers can recompute candidate equations at varying resolution. Scheme-independent complex patterns would confirm it, while patterns that are discretization artifacts would refute the published examples. Because the book already flags scheme sensitivity, a single gallery of pictures is not an adequate dataset, and a careful convergence study is more than a routine week's work.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-solve the specific simple partial differential equations Wolfram exhibits, under at least two independent discretizations with a convergence check, and test whether the complex patterns and discrete-looking patches survive. Scheme-independent complexity confirms the claim; patterns that disappear under refinement would refute those examples.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
There is no canonical sample of 'simple' partial differential equations, so existence is easier to support than to refute.

The book itself notes that some details of these solutions are sensitive to the numerical scheme.
